section.sectionSummaryBrief: The greatness of the future revelation is understood from the extraordinary divine service in this exile, which surpasses even Moshe's level.
section.t: And behold, the greatness of the elevation that will be in the future will be understood from the magnitude of the wonder of the divine service in this exile that precedes it — the preparation and introduction to it.
For it is known,
the statement of the Alter Rebbe in the name of the Baal Shem Tov on the verse,
"Indeed, in the Sanctuary I saw You" — would that I had seen You during the time of the Holy Temple.
And it is known
in the explanation of "And the man Moshe was exceedingly humble, more than any person on the face of the earth,"
that it was especially when Moshe saw the generation of the heels of Moshiach,
that there would then be many concealments and veils, etc., and despite all this they would study Torah and fulfill mitzvos, in a manner of increasing and adding light,
behold, this divine service brought about humility and self-nullification in Moshe.
And Moshe is truth,
and our sages said,
"He saw the attribute of truth,"
behold it is understood from this,
that it is indeed true,
that there is a superiority in the divine service of this exile
over the divine service of Moshe.
And from this is understood the greatness of the elevation that will be in the future,
since the revelation will be after and through such an elevated divine service.
And with this will also be understood the reason for the length of this exile,
for since this exile is an introduction to a most elevated revelation,
higher than the placement in the Garden of Eden of Adam HaRishon,
higher than the Giving of the Torah,
higher than the First Temple and the Second Temple,
therefore the exile is of such great length,
so that through the divine service of the Jewish people during the time of exile they will very soon reach the Third Temple,
which is a most elevated revelation,
"Surely, alone, the eye of Yaakov,"
"an inheritance without borders."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The word "Eichah" explains how the level of "Badad" is drawn down through the Seder Hishtalshelus in a settled manner.
section.t: And behold, in order that the aspect of "Badad" be drawn downward, and in a manner of "Yashvah" — settlement,
the drawing down must be through the levels of the order of the chain of descent.
And this is what is written, "Eichah yashvah badad,"
that the drawing down of the aspect of "Badad" below,
and in a manner of "Yashvah"
(in settlement),
is through "Eichah."
For behold, the letter Alef alludes to several levels, one after the other.
And like the Alef of "Echad" — the Alef that is above the Chet and Dalet,
[representing] the seven heavens and the earth and the four directions of the world — the Alef — the Master of the world,
but the Alef of "Eichah,"
the Alef is above the Yud — above the matter of the ten Sefiros,
(and it can be said that it is also above the hidden ten Sefiros),
and the Alef
is drawn into the Yud
(that is in "Eichah")
which alludes to the ten Sefiros of Atzilus,
and afterwards — the "Chaf-Hei"
(of "Eichah")
which refers to the aspect of Malchus, and specifically — Malchus as it is already related to or also — as it descends and becomes enclothed in Biyah.
And it is known
the difference between "Zeh" and "Choh,"
that "Zeh" is the matter of pointing with a finger and saying "this,"
and similarly is the term "Zos"
(which is also in the manner of the aspect of "Zeh,"
except that "Zos" is the feminine aspect),
which is the aspect of Malchus as it is in Atzilus,
and the aspect of "Choh" is the aspect of Malchus, and specifically — as it is enclothed in Biyah,
the aspect of "in our likeness."
And this is the matter of "Eichah yashvah badad,"
that "Badad" is the aspect of Yechidah, which is higher even than the aspect of Echad,
for the Alef here
(of "Eichah")
is — "One and there is no second, and He has no son or brother,"
the aspect of Atik, in which there is no division at all,
and as is known in Kabbalah
that the union
(of male waters and female waters)
that is in Atik is from within itself and within itself,
behold, in the future, the aspect of "Badad" will also be drawn down in revelation below and in settlement.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The word "Badad" contains two Dalets, representing the desire of the influencer to give and the recipient's need to receive, connected to the concept of prayer for the Divine "heaviness."
section.t: And behold, it is known the teaching of the Maggid of Mezeritch
that "Badad" has two Dalets.
A Dalet of the influencer and a Dalet of the recipient.
And at first glance,
behold, a Dalet is the matter of poverty,
"I am impoverished,"
and how can there be a Dalet of the influencer?
And it is explained there that it is like the saying of our sages,
"More than the calf wants to suck, the cow wants to nurse,"
meaning that there is a longing and desire in the influencer to influence the recipient,
and this is the Dalet of the influencer.
And perhaps this can be connected with what we learned regarding "You yearn for the work of Your hands."
And behold, just as the desire
(the Dalet)
of the influencer is that the lack of the recipient be filled,
so too the desire
(the Dalet)
of the recipient must be that the lack be filled,
so to speak,
of the influencer,
and as is known in the explanation of the Maggid of Mezeritch on the Mishnah, "One should not stand to pray except from a heavy-headed state,"
that prayer must be for the heaviness of head above,
that the Shechinah says,
"Woe is to Me from My head, woe is to Me from My arm."
And similarly is implied from the explanation of the Baal Shem Tov
on the verse,
"This I will recall to my heart, therefore I will hope,"
"This" — the Shechinah.
